name: Qualcomm OnQ blog: 'Qualcomm AI200 Accelerator for Generative AI' (Feb 2023)
notes: Qualcomm's own OnQ engineering blog introducing AI200, read via browser on 2026-10-03 (qualcomm.com serves almost nothing to web_extract - it gates on a Qualcomm ID - so the browser is required). Qualifies as a vendor primary source for the AI200's positioning but NOT for a spec table: it gives no TOPS figure, no memory capacity, no bus width and no TDP. Its substantive content is architectural and commercial: AI200 is described as supporting generative AI and LLMs at the data centre edge with a cloud-inference pricing model, and as building on the Hexagon AI/AI Engine lineage. Because it publishes no throughput number, it cannot be used to fill a flops row - which is exactly why the AI200 record's compute field stays null rather than being back-computed from the AI100's TOPS figure. NOTE the naming continuity trap: the chip is 'Qualcomm AI200' while the inference card is sold as the 'Qualcomm Cloud AI 100' family - Qualcomm kept the Cloud AI 100 card name for the AI200-based card, so 'Cloud AI 100 Ultra' and 'AI200' can refer to the same product generation and the repo should not treat them as two unrelated parts.
